requirement_text.REQ-432:
Follow-on to REQ-373 (service_catalog version/status lifecycle + real PinResolver.Lookup, status: done on the backend) and to REQ-399 (case-detail dependency-version/provenance screen, status: done -- REQ-399 already built the GET /api/v1/instances/{id}/pins route, web/src/hooks/useInstancePins.ts, and web/src/components/instances/InstancePinsPanel.tsx, wired into InstanceDetailPage.tsx). Filed from ISS-0898, split from ISS-0890's WF05-FULL-20260929 PLATFORM UAT report: the platform-instance-pin-survives-catalog-change scenario (test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/instance-pin-survives-catalog-change.yaml) is BLOCKED not because the read-only provenance screen is missing (REQ-399 built that) but because two operator ACTIONS the scenario's own steps exercise have no UI anywhere, and REQ-399's own SCOPE explicitly excluded one of them: "any UI affordance to CHANGE a pin from this screen... is a separate requirement if one is ever filed."
WHAT EXISTS TODAY, verified 2026-09-30 by direct source read: - `POST /api/v1/admin/services/:service_id/versions` (publish) and
  `POST /api/v1/admin/services/:service_id/retire` (retire) are real,
  shipped REQ-373 routes (lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex,
  design doc lib/letflow/design/req373-service-catalog-version-lifecycle.md
  §7), gated by the existing :AdminServicesManage permission. Grepping
  web/src/api/services.ts and web/src/pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx
  for "publish"/"retire"/"version" returns zero hits beyond the existing
  `ServiceRecord` type -- neither route has any frontend client function or
  UI control. An operator today cannot publish a new service-connection
  version or retire an old one from the GUI at all, which is exactly the
  scenario's own step 2 action.
- `POST /instances/:id/rebind-pins` is a real, shipped REQ-078/PIN-05 route
  (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex, `Letflow.Engine.PinRebind.rebind_pins/3`,
  200 response `{instance_id, changes, rebound_at}`, each change item
  carrying `ref`/`prior_version`/`new_version` per the
  `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND` event it appends). Grepping web/src for "rebind"
  returns zero hits beyond REQ-399's own read-only provenance panel and its
  test -- there is no rebind client function, no rebind action/button/dialog
  anywhere in web/src. An operator today cannot deliberately move a running
  case onto a different pinned version from the GUI at all, which is
  exactly the scenario's own step 5 action (with a caller-supplied reason
  -- `rebind_attrs()` requires `:idempotency_key`, per
  lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex's own design notes, and the scenario's
  step 5 input is `reason: \"External system retires the old endpoint at
  month end.\"`).
- Case history rendering: grepped web/src for any existing generic
  event-timeline renderer capable of showing an `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND`
  entry with actor/prior_version/new_version/reason (EO-005's own evidence
  requirement, "the case history shows the change with the operator's
  name, the previous and new version, and the reason given") -- confirm at
  implementation time whether InstanceDetailPage.tsx's existing
  history/timeline section already renders arbitrary event types generically
  (in which case this requirement only needs the rebind action itself to
  produce the right event, already true by construction since
  `rebind_pins/3` already appends the real event) or needs a
  dedicated case for this event type -- do not assume either way without
  checking.

THIS REQUIREMENT BUILDS: (1) a typed `publish`/`retire` client pair in web/src/api/services.ts and UI controls on web/src/pages/admin/services/ServicesPage.tsx (a "publish new version" action taking the publish_attrs() fields plus a version string, and a "retire" action) for a PLATFORM_ADMIN-equivalent operator; (2) a typed `rebind` client function (POST /instances/:id/rebind-pins) and a rebind action/dialog on REQ-399's InstancePinsPanel.tsx (or InstanceDetailPage.tsx) requiring the caller to supply a reason string, wired to the real endpoint; (3) confirm, and if needed extend, the case history/timeline rendering so an `INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND` entry's actor, prior_version, new_version and reason are all visible per EO-005; (4) the named pipeline_test spec.
OUT OF SCOPE: any change to `Letflow.ServiceCatalog`, `PinResolver`, `PinRebind`, or any of REQ-373/REQ-399's already-shipped routes (pure frontend consumption/action wiring against already-shipped endpoints); re-scoping or modifying REQ-399's read-only provenance display beyond what is needed to add the rebind action to the same screen; PLC-01/module_ref catalog versioning (still the identical, already-named SCOPE GAP pin_resolver.ex's own moduledoc states, unscoped to any stage, restated by both REQ-373 and REQ-399).

result.summary: FAIL. Design file lib/letflow/design/req432-rebind-pins-publish-retire-ui.md read in full (200 lines). No implementation bodies found; no literal TBD wording. Verified against source and CONFIRMED: publish/retire routes, body/status codes/response fields and :AdminServicesManage gate (lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex handle_publish/handle_retire/service_record_json); rebind route @rebind_schema, entry shape, Idempotency-Key header truncation/UUID fallback, :InstancesCancel gate, 200 shape and error mapping (lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex 338,437-522,1566-1670; lib/letflow/engine/pin_rebind.ex 445-480 payload {entries,actor,reason}); client.postWithHeaders exists (web/src/api/client.ts:262; precedent is onboarding.ts:114, design says :117, trivial); timeline finding F2 (timeline_item metadata != payload, description 'Instance pins rebound by <actor>', instances.ex 278,320-335) and F3/F4 (history_item_map omits actor_id, instances.ex:903-910; EventHistoryPanel falls back to 'system'); M4 (service_catalog.ex retire/1 retires only the single current row, publish/3 archives a retired current row unconditionally, so retire-then-publish IS achievable through the real backend and publish-then-retire would wrongly retire the new version). Checks FAILED: see issues. Route back to CODE-DESIGNER.
issues: FAIL [EO-005 / build item 3: 'actor, prior_version, new_version and reason are all visible'; EO-005 verification 'the case history shows the change with the operator's name, the previous and new version, and the reason given']: design §6 splits the evidence across two tabs: History tab shows versions+reason but only the actor UUID (and the same row's Actor column shows the literal 'system', per F4), Timeline tab shows the name but no versions/reason. No single case-history view shows name + prior + new + reason, and the History row shows a contradictory 'system' actor for a named operator. The design declares this adequate and leaves it as OQ-1 ('confirm with REQ owner whether one-tab display is required'), i.e. an open question on an AC-mapped element, contrary to the gate. A frontend-only remedy exists and was rejected without justification: the Timeline feed already returns event_id + actor_display_name (web/src/types/api.ts TimelineEntry; instances.ex timeline_item) so the History tab (or a combined view in InstanceDetailPage) can resolve actorLabel by event_id from the existing timeline query with no backend change. Rework: design the actor-name resolution (source query, matching key, fallback when absent) so that the INSTANCE_PINS_REBOUND history entry itself shows operator name, prior_version, new_version and reason, and make the pipeline step 06 assert all four on one view; drop OQ-1 as a deferral of this AC.

FAIL [EO-001/EO-004 'in-flight step' coverage, pipeline spec §7 steps pre and 03]: precondition mechanism for a live process definition with a catalog_entry pin and a service-task is deferred to OQ-4 ('this design does not prescribe it'), and step 03 ('let case A reach the service step ... completes the step without error') does not say how the service step executes against a registered service (endpoint_url reachability/outcome, which task to complete, which assertion proves the step ran). EO-001/EO-004 evidence explicitly requires 'the case history entry for the step performed at step 3', but OQ-9 leaves that history assertion unspecified and the design asserts only case status/pins panel. The AC 'retiring a version does not error or block the already-running case's pin display or in-flight step' is therefore only covered for pin display (step 04), not for the in-flight step. Rework: specify the concrete definition/fixture mechanism (read the definitions routes and db-exec helper now, it is resolvable from source), the service-step endpoint/expected outcome, and the exact history event type/assertion for step 3. Ordering itself (retire first, then publish) is verified achievable and is not the defect.

FAIL [build item 2 cache invalidation, §4.3 and §1]: §4.3 gives conditional/deferred instruction ('FRONTEND-DEV: if events/timeline key factories take extra filter/cursor args, invalidate by the shared prefix ... do not construct keys by hand') while §1 asserts 'No new query-key factory is needed'. Source resolves the condition: queryKeys.instances.events(tenantId,id,filters?) and timeline(tenantId,id,cursor,pageSize) (web/src/api/queryKeys.ts:97-100) take extra args and the tenant-scoped wrapper exposes no prefix-only form. Design must state the exact invalidation (e.g. instances.all() prefix as useCancelInstance does, or a named new prefix helper) rather than leave the choice to the implementer.

NOTE (non-blocking, fix in same rework): §4.3/§5.3 reuse an Idempotency-Key for retries while OQ-5 admits replay semantics were not verified; state the verified replay behaviour from EventStore.append or reduce the claim. Also minor citation drift: postWithHeaders precedent is web/src/api/onboarding.ts:114, not :117.
